sections.h2: Where is Cass County, Nebraska, and how did it start?
sections.html:
Cass County is bounded on the north by the Platte River and on the east by the Missouri River, with Plattsmouth as the county seat. The county's About page says the territorial legislature approved it on March 7, 1855, and named it for General Lewis Cass of Michigan. It measures roughly 34 miles east to west and 20 miles north to south.

Wikipedia gives a 2020 census population of 26,598 and a 2025 estimate of 27,657. Plattsmouth is the largest city. The town began in 1852 as a ferry point on the Missouri River, and its name comes from its position at the meeting of the Platte and Missouri.

The county describes itself as one of the earliest settled in Nebraska. Many early towns have since vanished, and fifteen remain.

sections.h2: Which towns are in Cass County?
sections.html:
The county lists fifteen towns, each with its own origin story on the About page:

  • Alvo, Avoca, Cedar Creek and Eagle
  • Elmwood, Greenwood, Louisville and Manley
  • Murdock, Murray, Nehawka and Plattsmouth
  • South Bend, Union and Weeping Water

Some have railroad roots. Alvo was a stop on the Rock Island route, and Murdock was named for a member of the town site company for the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad. Weeping Water takes its name from a creek the French called "the Water that Weeps."

Plattsmouth is the county seat and the largest city, and the other fourteen are towns and villages. A seller outside Plattsmouth still deals with the same county Assessor and Treasurer, all of them in Plattsmouth.

sections.h2: What offices handle property tax in Cass County?
sections.html:
The Assessor values property and the Treasurer collects the tax. The Assessor's office, at 145 N. 4th St. in Plattsmouth, is in the Annex just north of the courthouse, at the corner of N. 4th St. and Avenue A. It is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 402-296-9310.

The Treasurer's page gives the current address as 446 Main Street, 2nd floor, with the same Monday to Friday hours and a property tax line at 402-296-9511. The page flags that the office has moved, so confirm the location before you bring a payment.

  • A 24-hour drop box sits at 446 Main St on the northwest side of the building. Do not put cash in it.
  • The office takes cash, check, money order and cards (extra fees apply).
  • Online payments go through Nebraska Taxes Online at nto.us.
  • Cards are not accepted for tax sale redemptions.

The Assessor's page says the office handles about 21,000 real estate parcels and 1,300 personal property parcels, processes over 900 homestead applications and 150 permissive exemption applications, and answers about 10,000 information requests a year.

sections.h2: When is Cass County property tax late?
sections.html:
The tax sale notes put delinquency dates on May 1 and September 1. The Treasurer's tax sale notes say later years of delinquent tax become delinquent on May 1 and September 1.

These dates differ from Douglas County, which uses April 1 and August 1, so do not borrow another county's calendar. Always check the statement for the county that sends it.

Interest rates on delinquent tax come from state law. In Cass County's tax sale information, a buyer of a tax certificate is paid 14% simple interest from the sale date to the redemption date when the owner redeems.

sections.h2: What is the 2026 Cass County reappraisal?
sections.html:
The Assessor is doing its required six-year review in 2026, which will set values for 2027. The Assessor's page says data collectors will work from April through December 31, 2026, in these places:

  • Towns: Avoca, Manley, Nehawka, Union and Weeping Water villages
  • Rural townships: Mount Pleasant, Center, Weeping Water, Avoca/Nehawka and Nehawka/Liberty

Collectors wear orange reflective vests, carry county badges issued by the Sheriff's Office and drive county vehicles. They photograph and measure structures. If nobody is home, they leave a call-back slip on the door. Owners can return a property review questionnaire by mail or in the drop box on the west side of the courthouse.

If you own a house in one of those areas and plan to sell, a reappraisal visit is a good time to confirm that the square footage, finished basement and outbuildings on record match what is actually there. Errors in that record affect the value your future buyer will be taxed on.

sections.h2: How do I protest a property value in Cass County?
sections.html:
Use Form 422. The Assessor's page links Form 422 with instructions, and the county has a separate Property Valuation Protest page. The Assessor's page also links to the state's Tax Equalization and Review Commission for later steps.

Other deadlines on the Assessor's page:

  • Homestead exemption applications are due between February 2 and June 30.
  • Personal property filings are due on or before May 1.
  • The Assessor reviews applications for religious, charitable and educational exemptions.

The Assessor is an elected official with a four-year term and must hold a state certificate and complete 15 hours of continuing education each year.

sections.h2: How does the Cass County tax sale work?
sections.html:
It is an auction of tax lien certificates held on the first Monday in March. The county's 2025 information sheet says the sale ran at the Plattsmouth Community Center, 308 S. 18th St., starting at 8 a.m., and that delinquent taxes are advertised for three weeks in February in the Sarpy County Times.

  • Buyers pay a $25 registration fee and $20 per certificate.
  • The sale uses a round robin format, where a random first bidder gets the first parcel.
  • Buyers acquire a lien, not the property, and they cannot foreclose for three years.
  • The Treasurer does not issue treasurer's deeds, so foreclosure goes through the courts.
  • Parcels already on a tax sale, in bankruptcy, or owned by government are not sold.

The notice states that published amounts do not include delinquent interest and may cover several years. If your house is on the list, get a current payoff in writing, because a sale to a buyer lets the title company clear the amount at closing.

sections.h2: What happens at closing when a Cass County house sells?
sections.html:
The Nebraska documentary stamp tax applies to the deed. The Department of Revenue's regulations put the rate at $2.25 per $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, state that the grantor is liable, and allow the grantee or any agent presenting the deed to pay it. Deeds are recorded through the Cass County Register of Deeds, which has an online deed search.

The Assessor's office also keeps a sales file for every property sale in the county and checks it against its records, according to its services list. That file is one reason an unusually low sale price may draw a data collector's visit later, which is worth knowing if you are pricing a quick as-is sale.

Cash Home Buyers can look at a Cass County house with unpaid tax, a reappraisal question or a lien, and give a written offer. The title company confirms payoffs before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Cass County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the Treasurer's office, 446 Main Street, 2nd floor, Plattsmouth, in the drop box, or online through Nebraska Taxes Online. Cards carry extra fees and are not accepted for tax sale redemptions.

faqs.q: When does Cass County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's tax sale notes give May 1 and September 1 as the delinquency dates.
Yes. The Assessor is doing its six-year review in 2026 for 2027 values, with data collectors working from April through December 31 in named villages and townships.

faqs.q: What form do I use to protest a Cass County valuation?
faqs.a: Form 422, which the Assessor's page links with instructions. The county also has a Property Valuation Protest page.

faqs.q: Does Cass County issue treasurer's deeds after a tax sale?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's notice says no. A certificate holder must foreclose through the courts, and there are statutory time limits on certificates.
